subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Unit 2 – Lesson 3: Grammar 1 (there is / there are with countable and uncountable nouns)
outcomes: Use there is / there are with a lot of, some, a few and a little.
Tell countable nouns from uncountable nouns.

tf.s: We say: There are a few sandwiches.
tf.why: Yes! Sandwiches are countable, so we use a few.

tf.s: We say: There is a few lemonade.
tf.why: Lemonade is uncountable: There is a little lemonade.
Correct! We say There isn't any bread.
We can count grapes, so they are countable.

tf.s: We say: There are a lot of noodles.
tf.why: Great! Noodles is plural, so we use are.

tf.s: 'There are a little vegetables' is correct.
tf.why: Vegetables are countable: There are a few vegetables.
Well done! We say a little tea, a little salad.

tf.s: We say: There aren't any bread.
tf.why: Bread is uncountable: There isn't any bread.

boxes.q: Make it negative: There are some cupcakes.
In Picture A, there ___ a few crisps.

hunt.q: Countable: a few or a little?
Uncountable: a few or a little?

mcq.q: Which word goes with countable nouns?
mcq.why: We say a few sandwiches, a few grapes.

mcq.q: Which word goes with uncountable nouns?
mcq.why: We say a little lemonade, a little tea.

o: There are a lot of cupcakes.

mcq.q: Which list has only uncountable nouns?
mcq.why: We can't count tea, salad or lemonade.

mcq.q: Sort: grapes, tea, salad, crisps. Which are countable?
mcq.why: We can count grapes and crisps.

mcq.q: Picture A has a lot of tea. Picture B has some tea. Choose the correct sentence.
o: In Picture A, there is a lot of tea.
In Picture A, there are a lot of tea.
In Picture B, there is a lot of tea.
In Picture A, there is a few tea.

mcq.q: Why do we say 'There isn't any bread' and not 'There aren't any bread'?
o: Bread is uncountable, so we use is.

mcq.q: Why do we say 'a few sandwiches' but 'a little lemonade'?
o: We can count sandwiches but not lemonade.
mcq.why: Great! a few for countable, a little for uncountable.

mcq.q: In Picture A there isn't any salad. In Picture B there is a little salad. What is the difference?
o: Picture B has some salad; Picture A has none.
Both have a lot of salad.
mcq.why: A little is more than none.
